title: CDFs, Medians and Percentiles
short: F(x) = ∫ f(t) dt from −∞ to x, f = F′, and the median m solves F(m) = 1/2.
trouble: Students build F(x) for a piecewise density from the current piece alone, leaving out the area of the pieces to its left.

blocks.html: The CDF $F(x) = P(X \le x)$ works for every random variable. For a continuous one it is the area under the density to the left of $x$, and the first part of the Fundamental Theorem connects the two: the density is the CDF's rate of change.
$$F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)\,dt, \qquad F'(x) = f(x), \qquad P(a < X \le b) = F(b) - F(a).$$ The median $m$ solves $F(m) = \frac{1}{2}$; the $p$th percentile solves $F(x_p) = p$.

$F(x)$ is an accumulation function of the density, so by the Fundamental Theorem it is continuous and $F' = f$ wherever $f$ is continuous. $F$ rises from 0 to 1 and never decreases, because the area keeps adding nonnegative pieces. For a density given in pieces, $F(x)$ must include all the area to the left of $x$, including whole earlier pieces.

blocks.name: prob-density
blocks.cap: A triangle-shaped density in two pieces, with its CDF. The CDF at any point includes all the area to its left; the median sits where the CDF reaches one half.

blocks.title: A density in two pieces
blocks.q: $f(x) = x$ on $[0, 1]$ and $f(x) = 2 - x$ on $[1, 2]$. Find $F(1.5)$, and a formula for $F$ on $[1, 2]$.
steps: The whole left piece has area $\int_{0}^{1} x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}$.

blocks.title: From the CDF back to the density
blocks.q: $F(x) = 1 - e^{-x/2}$ for $x \ge 0$ (and 0 for $x < 0$). Find the density and the median.

blocks.html: Building $F(x)$ on a later piece from that piece alone, for example $\int_{1}^{x}(2 - t)\,dt$, and forgetting the $\frac{1}{2}$ of area already to the left. Check the joins: $F$ must be continuous, so its formula on each piece has to agree with the previous piece at the boundary, and the last piece must end at 1.
